Supplementary global analysis code

analysis/09_global_moran.R adds global permutation tests, the scatterplot and the eight-setting sensitivity table without changing the original local, EHSA or robustness outputs. Its cache tracks the upstream signatures and its own source. Checks cover township alignment, the direct Moran formula, scatterplot slope, both Holm families, graph symmetry and repeated permutations. The earlier clean-directory verification below predates this stage.

 # Adapt the Hands-on 5(1) global test and 5(2) centred scatterplot workflow.
# Reuse the existing township order and repaired queen graph; do not change EHSA.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(spdep);library(sf);library(dplyr);library(ggplot2)})
d <- readRDS('outputs/prepared.rds')
s <- readRDS('outputs/statistics.rds')
g <- d$townships
stopifnot(identical(as.character(attr(s$nb,'region.id')),as.character(g$TS_PCODE)),
          all(card(s$nb)>0))
w <- nb2listw(s$nb,style='W',zero.policy=FALSE)
n <- nrow(g)
B <- 9999L
rows <- points <- list()
tests <- list()
for(v in c('events','fatalities')) {
  x <- g[[v]]
  stopifnot(length(x)==n,all(is.finite(x)),sd(x)>0)
  z <- as.numeric(scale(x))
  lag_z <- lag.listw(w,z,zero.policy=FALSE)
  seed <- if(v=='events') 2026102101L else 2026102102L
  set.seed(seed)
  mc <- moran.mc(x,w,nsim=B,alternative='two.sided',zero.policy=FALSE)
  # Explicit inclusive tails with a +1 correction avoid a zero Monte Carlo p.
  simulated <- mc$res[seq_len(B)]
  observed <- as.numeric(mc$statistic)
  permutation_p <- min(1,2*min((1+sum(simulated>=observed))/(B+1),
                              (1+sum(simulated<=observed))/(B+1)))
  # Independent algebraic check: S0 = n for these non-isolated W weights.
  slope <- sum(z*lag_z)/sum(z*z)
  direct_I <- (n/Szero(w))*slope
  stopifnot(abs(Szero(w)-n)<1e-10,abs(direct_I-as.numeric(mc$statistic))<1e-12)
  local <- s$static %>% filter(variable==v)
  q <- local$moran_q[match(g$TS_PCODE,local$code)]
  quadrant <- case_when(z>0 & lag_z>0~'High-High',z<0 & lag_z<0~'Low-Low',
                        z>0 & lag_z<0~'High-Low',z<0 & lag_z>0~'Low-High',TRUE~'On mean')
  rows[[v]] <- data.frame(variable=v,n=n,I=direct_I,null_expectation=-1/(n-1),
                          permutation_p=permutation_p,permutations=B,seed=seed,slope=slope)
  points[[v]] <- data.frame(code=g$TS_PCODE,variable=v,z=z,lag_z=lag_z,
                            quadrant=quadrant,local_q=q,
                            local_support=ifelse(q<.05,'Local BH q < 0.05','Other townships'))
  tests[[v]] <- mc
}
results <- bind_rows(rows)
results$holm_p <- p.adjust(results$permutation_p,method='holm')
# Cross two representations with two graphs for each outcome. Keep all eight
# comparisons in one Holm family, including the original raw/queen results.
xy <- st_coordinates(st_point_on_surface(g))
kn6 <- make.sym.nb(knn2nb(knearneigh(xy,k=6),row.names=g$TS_PCODE))
graphs <- list(Queen=s$nb,`Symmetric 6-NN`=kn6)
sensitivity_rows <- list()
for(v in c('events','fatalities')) for(graph_name in names(graphs)) for(transform in c('Raw','log1p')) {
  x <- if(transform=='Raw') g[[v]] else log1p(g[[v]])
  sw <- nb2listw(graphs[[graph_name]],style='W',zero.policy=FALSE)
  base <- results[results$variable==v,]
  # The same seed within an outcome pairs the random reallocations across settings.
  set.seed(base$seed)
  mc <- moran.mc(x,sw,nsim=B,alternative='two.sided',zero.policy=FALSE)
  null <- mc$res[seq_len(B)]
  obs <- as.numeric(mc$statistic)
  pv <- min(1,2*min((1+sum(null>=obs))/(B+1),(1+sum(null<=obs))/(B+1)))
  centered <- x-mean(x)
  direct <- n/Szero(sw)*sum(centered*lag.listw(sw,centered))/sum(centered^2)
  stopifnot(abs(obs-direct)<1e-12)
  sensitivity_rows[[length(sensitivity_rows)+1L]] <- data.frame(variable=v,
    graph=graph_name,transform=transform,I=obs,permutation_p=pv,
    permutations=B,seed=base$seed,min_neighbours=min(card(graphs[[graph_name]])),
    max_neighbours=max(card(graphs[[graph_name]])))
}
sensitivity <- bind_rows(sensitivity_rows)
sensitivity$holm_p_8 <- p.adjust(sensitivity$permutation_p,'holm')
sensitivity$positive_supported <- sensitivity$I>0 & sensitivity$holm_p_8<.05
scatter <- bind_rows(points)
labels <- setNames(sprintf('%s\nGlobal I = %.3f',c('Event counts','Reported fatalities'),results$I),results$variable)
palette <- c('High-High'='#b2182b','Low-Low'='#2166ac','High-Low'='#ef8a62','Low-High'='#67a9cf','On mean'='#777777')
p <- ggplot(scatter,aes(z,lag_z))+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0,colour='grey65',linetype='dashed')+
  geom_vline(xintercept=0,colour='grey65',linetype='dashed')+
  geom_abline(data=results,aes(slope=slope,intercept=0),colour='#222222',linewidth=.65)+
  geom_point(aes(colour=quadrant,shape=local_support),size=2.3,alpha=.8)+
  facet_wrap(~variable,labeller=as_labeller(labels))+
  scale_colour_manual(values=palette)+
  scale_shape_manual(values=c('Local BH q < 0.05'=17,'Other townships'=1))+
  labs(title='Overall spatial association and local quadrants',
       subtitle='330 townships; January 2021 to September 2025; unchanged queen-based W weights',
       x='Standardised township total (z)',y='Spatial lag of the same z',colour='Descriptive quadrant',shape='Existing local Moran test',
       caption='Lines pass through the origin with slope I. Colour alone does not imply significance.\nTriangles use existing outcome-specific BH-adjusted local tests, not the global p-values.')+
  theme_minimal(base_size=12)+theme(legend.position='bottom',panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
    plot.title=element_text(face='bold'),plot.caption=element_text(hjust=0))+
  guides(colour=guide_legend(nrow=1,order=1),shape=guide_legend(nrow=1,order=2))
dir.create('outputs/figures',recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
ggsave('outputs/figures/global_moran_scatter.png',p,width=11,height=7,dpi=160,bg='white')
saveRDS(list(results=results,scatter=scatter,tests=tests,sensitivity=sensitivity,
            sensitivity_graphs=graphs),'outputs/global_moran.rds')
write.csv(results,'outputs/global_moran_summary.csv',row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(sensitivity,'outputs/global_moran_sensitivity.csv',row.names=FALSE)
print(results)
print(sensitivity)

Efficient conditional-simulation helper

A fresh statistical rebuild requires Rcpp and an R-compatible C++ compiler, such as Rtools on Windows. The rejection sampler retains the conditional, without-replacement reference model; it does not lower the number of simulations. Cached rendering does not require recompiling it.

 # Exact conditional sampling without replacement for sparse space-time graphs.
# Rejection sampling avoids repeatedly shuffling the entire 18,810-bin population.
# Compilation requires Rcpp and an R-compatible C++ toolchain (Rtools on Windows).
Rcpp::cppFunction(code='
Rcpp::NumericMatrix conditional_gi_sample(Rcpp::NumericVector x,
    Rcpp::List neighbours, Rcpp::List weights, int nsim) {
  int n=x.size();
  Rcpp::NumericMatrix out(n,3);
  for(int i=0;i<n;i++) {
    Rcpp::IntegerVector ids=neighbours[i];
    Rcpp::NumericVector w=weights[i];
    int k=ids.size();
    double observed=0.0, fixed=0.0;
    std::vector<double> other_weights;
    for(int j=0;j<k;j++) {
      observed+=w[j]*x[ids[j]-1];
      if(ids[j]-1==i) fixed+=w[j]*x[i];
      else other_weights.push_back(w[j]);
    }
    int m=other_weights.size();
    std::vector<int> selected(m);
    int lower=0,upper=0; double total=0.0,total2=0.0;
    for(int b=0;b<nsim;b++) {
      double value=fixed;
      for(int j=0;j<m;j++) {
        int draw; bool duplicate;
        do {
          draw=(int)floor(R::runif(0.0,(double)(n-1)));
          if(draw>=i)draw++;
          duplicate=false;
          for(int h=0;h<j;h++)if(selected[h]==draw){duplicate=true;break;}
        } while(duplicate);
        selected[j]=draw;value+=other_weights[j]*x[draw];
      }
      double tolerance=1e-10*std::max(1.0,std::abs(observed));
      if(value<=observed+tolerance)lower++;
      if(value>=observed-tolerance)upper++;
      total+=value;total2+=value*value;
    }
    out(i,0)=std::min(1.0,2.0*(1.0+std::min(lower,upper))/(nsim+1.0));
    out(i,1)=total/nsim;
    out(i,2)=(total2-total*total/nsim)/(nsim-1.0);
    if(i%100==0)Rcpp::checkUserInterrupt();
  }
  return out;
}')
fast_space_time_gi <- function(x,w,nsim=999L,seed=20261018L){
  stopifnot(is.numeric(x),all(is.finite(x)),length(x)==length(w$neighbours),nsim>=99L)
  set.seed(seed)
  sampled<-conditional_gi_sample(x,w$neighbours,w$weights,nsim)
  # Analytical Gi* z-values describe clustering strength; inference uses the
  # conditional randomisation distribution with the focal observation fixed.
  list(z=as.numeric(spdep::localG(x,w,zero.policy=TRUE)),p=sampled[,1],null_mean=sampled[,2],null_variance=sampled[,3])
}

Extended analysis and verification

analysis/04_extensions.R implements temporal sensitivity, hotspot-set comparisons, the conditional severity test and deterministic case selection. analysis/05_extension_figures.R generates the corresponding figures. analysis/06_evidence_audit.R diagnoses name flags, recomputes static sensitivity results, calculates national-share benchmarks and decomposes supported severity cases. analysis/07_evidence_figures.R draws these additional results. analysis/08_severity_validation.R repeats the preselected severity cases across seeds and largest-record deletion scenarios, retaining full-family adjustment. The stage cache includes these scripts so changed analytical choices invalidate dependent outputs. analysis/test_analysis.R checks pattern boundaries, raw-data fingerprints, count reconciliation, map masks, name-audit accounting, national-share identities, additive severity decompositions, deletion accounting and a small-graph exhaustive comparison for the Gi* sampler. These internal tests complement, rather than replace, independent methodological review.

From the exercise directory, Rscript --vanilla analysis/test_analysis.R runs the checks after a build. Rscript --vanilla -e "Sys.setenv(TH02_REBUILD='1'); source('analysis/run_analysis.R')" rebuilds all stages. Required package versions and external spatial-library versions are recorded below; they document the tested environment rather than claiming compatibility with every package version. On Windows, Rcpp also requires a working Rtools toolchain. For non-ASCII temporary-path issues, set TMPDIR to an existing writable ASCII-only directory before starting R.

A separate-directory verification copied only source files and raw inputs before starting the complete analysis without any existing outputs or stage cache. Preparation, core statistics, extensions, evidence audits, severity validation and figure-data objects matched the project outputs at a numerical tolerance of 1e-12. Raw-input fingerprints matched and the automated checks passed. Both runs used the same installed R environment, so this verifies independence from cached results rather than portability to another machine or independent validation of the source data. To repeat the check, copy the required sources, styles and locally authorised data to an empty directory, run Rscript --vanilla analysis/run_analysis.R, then run the tests and render the report.

04_extensions.R

# Additional uncertainty checks and explanatory cases. Raw data are read only.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr);library(tidyr);library(sf);library(spdep);library(Kendall)})
d <- readRDS('outputs/prepared.rds')
s <- readRDS('outputs/statistics.rds')
g <- d$townships
n <- nrow(g); nt <- length(d$months)
# Reuse the authoritative functions without executing the statistical pipeline.
for(expr in parse('analysis/02_statistics.R')) {
  if(is.call(expr) && identical(expr[[1]],as.name('<-')) && is.symbol(expr[[2]]) &&
     as.character(expr[[2]]) %in% c('classify_pattern','local_results')) eval(expr)
}
source('analysis/fast_gi.R')

sen_slope <- function(y) {
  ij <- combn(seq_along(y),2)
  median((y[ij[2,]]-y[ij[1,]])/(ij[2,]-ij[1,]))
}
mk_result <- function(y) {
  if(length(unique(y))<2L) return(c(tau=0,p=1))
  a <- Kendall::MannKendall(y)
  if(!is.finite(a$sl)) return(c(tau=0,p=1))
  c(tau=as.numeric(a$tau),p=as.numeric(a$sl))
}
block_test <- function(y,width,B=999L,seed=20261018L) {
  set.seed(seed)
  blocks <- split(seq_along(y),ceiling(seq_along(y)/width))
  observed <- mk_result(y)[['tau']]
  null <- replicate(B,mk_result(y[unlist(blocks[sample.int(length(blocks))])])[['tau']])
  (1+sum(abs(null)>=abs(observed)-1e-12))/(B+1)
}
space_time_weights <- function(nb,lag,n,nt) {
  out <- vector('list',n*nt)
  for(t in seq_len(nt)) for(i in seq_len(n)) {
    spatial <- sort(unique(c(i,nb[[i]][nb[[i]]>0])))
    out[[(t-1L)*n+i]] <- sort(as.integer(unlist(lapply(seq.int(max(1,t-lag),t),function(j)(j-1L)*n+spatial))))
  }
  class(out)<-'nb';attr(out,'region.id')<-as.character(seq_along(out))
  attr(out,'type')<-'space-time';attr(out,'sym')<-FALSE;attr(out,'self.included')<-TRUE
  nb2listw(out,style='W',zero.policy=TRUE)
}
summarise_cube <- function(z,p,variable,scenario) {
  zm<-matrix(z,nrow=n);pm<-matrix(p,nrow=n)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n),function(i){
    mk<-mk_result(zm[i,])
    cl<-classify_pattern(zm[i,],pm[i,],mk[['tau']],mk[['p']])
    tibble(code=g$TS_PCODE[i],variable=variable,scenario=scenario,
           tau=mk[['tau']],mk_p=mk[['p']],classification=cl,
           map_class=ifelse(mk[['p']]<.05 && cl!='No pattern detected',cl,'Not displayed'))
  }))
}

temporal <- list(); lag_results <- list(); bin_adjusted <- list(); slopes <- list()
for(v in c('events','fatalities')) {
  message('Trend robustness: ',v)
  gi<-s$gis %>% filter(variable==v)
  stopifnot(identical(gi$township_id,d$panel$township_id),identical(gi$month,d$panel$month))
  zm<-matrix(gi$gi_z,nrow=n);xm<-matrix(d$panel[[v]],nrow=n)
  baseline<-s$ehsa %>% filter(variable==v)
  temporal[[v]]<-bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n),function(i){
    tibble(code=g$TS_PCODE[i],variable=v,block_3=baseline$block_p[i],
      block_6=block_test(zm[i,],6,seed=20262000L+i),
      block_12=block_test(zm[i,],12,seed=20263000L+i),
      lag1_acf=as.numeric(acf(zm[i,],plot=FALSE,lag.max=1)$acf[2]))
  }))
  slopes[[v]]<-tibble(code=g$TS_PCODE,variable=v,
    gi_slope=apply(zm,1,sen_slope),count_slope=apply(xm,1,sen_slope))
  bin_adjusted[[v]]<-summarise_cube(gi$gi_z,gi$q,v,'BH-adjusted space-time bins')
  for(lag in c(0L,2L)) {
    message('Alternative time neighbourhood: ',v,', lag ',lag)
    w<-space_time_weights(s$nb,lag,n,nt)
    result<-fast_space_time_gi(d$panel[[v]],w,nsim=999L,seed=20261018L)
    lag_results[[paste(v,lag)]]<-summarise_cube(result$z,result$p,v,paste0('Previous months: ',lag))
  }
}
temporal<-bind_rows(temporal);lag_results<-bind_rows(lag_results)
bin_adjusted<-bind_rows(bin_adjusted);slopes<-bind_rows(slopes)
checks<-s$ehsa %>% left_join(temporal,by=c('code','variable')) %>% left_join(slopes,by=c('code','variable')) %>%
  mutate(all_blocks=block_3<.05 & block_6<.05 & block_12<.05,
         trend_supported=mk_p<.05 & mk_q<.05 & all_blocks,
         evidence=case_when(map_class=='Not displayed'~'No displayed trend-pattern',
           trend_supported~'BH and all block checks',TRUE~'Sensitivity-dependent pattern'))
temporal_summary<-checks %>% group_by(variable) %>% summarise(nominal=sum(mk_p<.05),
  block_3=sum(mk_p<.05 & block_3<.05),block_6=sum(mk_p<.05 & block_6<.05),
  block_12=sum(mk_p<.05 & block_12<.05),BH_and_all_blocks=sum(trend_supported),
  displayed=sum(map_class!='Not displayed'),supported_displayed=sum(map_class!='Not displayed' & trend_supported),.groups='drop')

comparison<-bind_rows(lag_results,bin_adjusted) %>%
  left_join(s$ehsa %>% select(code,variable,baseline_class=classification,baseline_map=map_class),by=c('code','variable'))
scenario_summary<-comparison %>% group_by(variable,scenario) %>% summarise(
  class_agreement=mean(classification==baseline_class),
  displayed=sum(map_class!='Not displayed'),
  retained_same_pattern=sum(map_class==baseline_map & baseline_map!='Not displayed'),
  baseline_displayed=sum(baseline_map!='Not displayed'),.groups='drop')

# Extend the original spatial sensitivity checks to the second outcome.
xy<-st_coordinates(st_point_on_surface(g));kn6<-make.sym.nb(knn2nb(knearneigh(xy,k=6)))
lw<-nb2listw(s$nb,style='W',zero.policy=TRUE);star<-nb2listw(include.self(s$nb),style='W',zero.policy=TRUE)
precise<-d$assigned %>% filter(geo_precision==1) %>% group_by(township_id) %>% summarise(fatalities=sum(fatalities),.groups='drop')
near<-d$unassigned %>% filter(match_count==0,nearest_m<=1000) %>% group_by(nearest_id) %>% summarise(fatalities=sum(fatalities),.groups='drop')
sens_fatalities<-bind_rows(
 bind_cols(tibble(scenario='Six-nearest-neighbour graph',code=g$TS_PCODE),local_results(g$fatalities,nb2listw(kn6,style='W'),nb2listw(include.self(kn6),style='W'))),
 bind_cols(tibble(scenario='Precisely located events only',code=g$TS_PCODE),local_results(replace_na(precise$fatalities[match(g$TS_PCODE,precise$township_id)],0),lw,star)),
 bind_cols(tibble(scenario='Add records within 1 km of boundary',code=g$TS_PCODE),local_results(g$fatalities+replace_na(near$fatalities[match(g$TS_PCODE,near$nearest_id)],0),lw,star)))
spatial<-bind_rows(mutate(s$sensitivity,variable='events'),mutate(sens_fatalities,variable='fatalities')) %>%
 left_join(s$static %>% select(code,variable,baseline_hotspot=hotspot),by=c('code','variable'))
spatial_summary<-spatial %>% group_by(variable,scenario) %>% summarise(
 baseline_hot=sum(baseline_hotspot=='Hot spot'),alternative_hot=sum(hotspot=='Hot spot'),
 retained=sum(hotspot=='Hot spot' & baseline_hotspot=='Hot spot'),
 gained=sum(hotspot=='Hot spot' & baseline_hotspot!='Hot spot'),
 lost=sum(hotspot!='Hot spot' & baseline_hotspot=='Hot spot'),
 Jaccard=sum(hotspot=='Hot spot' & baseline_hotspot=='Hot spot')/sum(hotspot=='Hot spot' | baseline_hotspot=='Hot spot'),.groups='drop')

# Value-added question: where do frequency and fatality concentration disagree?
# Use separately BH-adjusted Gi* families. No ranking of individual risk is implied.
ev<-s$static %>% filter(variable=='events') %>% select(code,event_z=gi_z,event_q=gi_q)
fa<-s$static %>% filter(variable=='fatalities') %>% select(code,fatality_z=gi_z,fatality_q=gi_q)
concordance<-inner_join(ev,fa,by='code') %>%
 mutate(event_hot=event_z>0 & event_q<.05,fatality_hot=fatality_z>0 & fatality_q<.05,
  category=case_when(event_hot & fatality_hot~'Both outcomes',event_hot~'Events only',fatality_hot~'Fatalities only',TRUE~'Neither outcome')) %>%
 left_join(st_drop_geometry(g) %>% select(code=TS_PCODE,township=TS,region=ST,events,fatalities),by='code')
concordance_summary<-concordance %>% group_by(category) %>% summarise(townships=n(),events=sum(events),fatalities=sum(fatalities),.groups='drop')
joint_stability<-spatial %>% mutate(hot=gi_z>0 & gi_q<.05) %>% select(code,variable,scenario,hot) %>%
 pivot_wider(names_from=variable,values_from=hot) %>%
 left_join(concordance %>% select(code,baseline_both=category),by='code') %>% group_by(scenario) %>%
 summarise(both=sum(events & fatalities),retained_baseline_both=sum(events & fatalities & baseline_both=='Both outcomes'),.groups='drop')

# Conditional spatial random-labelling test of incident severity.
# Hold incident locations, months and types fixed. Shuffle fatality marks only
# within month x event-type strata, preserving each stratum's fatality distribution.
# The self-including queen graph aggregates marks into local neighbourhoods.
severity_test <- function(records,scenario,B=999L,seed=20264000L) {
  idx<-match(records$township_id,g$TS_PCODE)
  aggregate_town<-function(x) as.numeric(rowsum(c(x,rep(0,n)),c(idx,seq_len(n)),reorder=TRUE))
  strata<-split(seq_len(nrow(records)),interaction(records$month,records$event_type,drop=TRUE))
  marks<-records$fatalities
  expected_marks<-marks
  for(ids in strata) expected_marks[ids]<-mean(marks[ids])
  adjacency<-nb2mat(include.self(s$nb),style='B',zero.policy=TRUE)
  observed<-as.numeric(adjacency %*% aggregate_town(marks))
  expected<-as.numeric(adjacency %*% aggregate_town(expected_marks))
  upper<-integer(n)
  set.seed(seed)
  for(b in seq_len(B)) {
    shuffled<-marks
    for(ids in strata) shuffled[ids]<-marks[ids[sample.int(length(ids))]]
    simulated<-as.numeric(adjacency %*% aggregate_town(shuffled))
    upper<-upper+as.integer(simulated>=observed)
  }
  p<-(upper+1)/(B+1)
  tibble(code=g$TS_PCODE,scenario=scenario,neighbourhood_events=as.numeric(adjacency %*% aggregate_town(rep(1,length(idx)))),
    observed=observed,expected=expected,ratio=ifelse(expected>0,observed/expected,NA_real_),p=p,q=p.adjust(p,'BH'))
}
message('Conditional severity permutation, all assigned events')
severity<-severity_test(d$assigned,'All assigned events')
message('Conditional severity permutation, precision code 1')
severity_precise<-severity_test(filter(d$assigned,geo_precision==1),'Precision code 1')
severity<-severity %>% left_join(severity_precise %>% select(code,precise_ratio=ratio,precise_q=q),by='code') %>%
 left_join(concordance %>% select(code,township,region,category),by='code') %>%
 mutate(excess=q<.05 & observed>expected,precise_excess=precise_q<.05 & precise_ratio>1)
write.csv(severity,'outputs/conditional_severity.csv',row.names=FALSE)

# Contrastive, reproducible selection. These four examples are not a random sample.
case_pool<-concordance %>% left_join(checks %>% filter(variable=='events') %>%
 select(code,classification,map_class,trend_supported),by='code')
used<-character();cases<-list()
choose_case<-function(pool,role,rankvar='events') {
  a<-pool %>% filter(!code %in% used) %>% arrange(desc(.data[[rankvar]]),code) %>% slice_head(n=1)
  stopifnot(nrow(a)==1)
  used<<-c(used,a$code);a$selection_reason<-role;a
}
cases[[1]]<-choose_case(filter(case_pool,map_class=='Oscillating hot spot'),'Largest event total among displayed oscillating event hot spots')
cases[[2]]<-choose_case(filter(case_pool,map_class=='Sporadic hot spot'),'Largest event total among displayed sporadic event hot spots')
cases[[3]]<-choose_case(filter(case_pool,map_class=='Not displayed'),'Largest event total without a displayed event trend-pattern')
cases[[4]]<-choose_case(filter(case_pool,category=='Fatalities only'),'Largest fatality total among fatality-only BH hot spots','fatalities')
cases<-bind_rows(cases) %>% mutate(case_id=paste0('Case ',row_number()))
case_stats<-checks %>% filter(code %in% cases$code) %>%
 left_join(cases %>% select(code,case_id,township,region,selection_reason),by='code')
case_trends<-d$panel %>% filter(township_id %in% cases$code) %>%
 pivot_longer(c(events,fatalities),names_to='variable',values_to='value') %>%
 left_join(s$gis,by=c('township_id','month','variable')) %>%
 left_join(cases %>% select(township_id=code,case_id,township,region),by='township_id')
matched_period<-case_trends %>% filter(format(month,'%Y') %in% c('2024','2025'),as.integer(format(month,'%m'))<=9) %>%
 group_by(township_id,variable,year=format(month,'%Y')) %>% summarise(total=sum(value),.groups='drop') %>%
 pivot_wider(names_from=year,values_from=total,names_prefix='Jan_Sep_') %>%
 mutate(absolute_change=Jan_Sep_2025-Jan_Sep_2024,
        percentage_change=ifelse(Jan_Sep_2024>0,100*absolute_change/Jan_Sep_2024,NA_real_))
case_stats<-case_stats %>% left_join(matched_period,by=c('code'='township_id','variable'))
saveRDS(list(checks=checks,temporal_summary=temporal_summary,comparison=comparison,scenario_summary=scenario_summary,
 spatial=spatial,spatial_summary=spatial_summary,concordance=concordance,concordance_summary=concordance_summary,
 joint_stability=joint_stability,severity=severity,cases=cases,case_stats=case_stats,case_trends=case_trends),'outputs/extensions.rds')
write.csv(checks,'outputs/trend_robustness.csv',row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(comparison,'outputs/ehsa_sensitivity.csv',row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(spatial_summary,'outputs/hotspot_stability.csv',row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(concordance,'outputs/outcome_concordance.csv',row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(case_stats,'outputs/township_cases.csv',row.names=FALSE)

# Diagnose naming flags, separate national change, and profile stable severity cases.
# Only aggregated outputs are saved. Raw incident records are never modified.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr);library(tidyr);library(sf);library(spdep)})
d<-readRDS('outputs/prepared.rds');s<-readRDS('outputs/statistics.rds');e<-readRDS('outputs/extensions.rds')
g<-d$townships;n<-nrow(g)
for(expr in parse('analysis/02_statistics.R')) {
 if(is.call(expr) && identical(expr[[1]],as.name('<-')) && is.symbol(expr[[2]]) &&
    as.character(expr[[2]])=='local_results')eval(expr)
}
normalise_name<-function(x)gsub('[^a-z0-9]','',tolower(x))
lookup<-st_drop_geometry(g) %>% transmute(code=TS_PCODE,name=TS,region=ST,
 key=normalise_name(TS),base_key=normalise_name(sub(' *\\(.*$','',TS)),region_key=normalise_name(ST))
a<-d$assigned %>% select(-region) %>% left_join(lookup %>% select(code,name,region),by=c('township_id'='code')) %>%
 mutate(name_missing=is.na(admin3)|trimws(admin3)=='',
 exact_match=!name_missing & tolower(trimws(admin3))==tolower(trimws(name)),
 name_flag=!exact_match,key=normalise_name(admin3),region_key=normalise_name(admin1))
candidate_code<-function(key,region_key) {
 if(is.na(key)||key=='')return(NA_character_)
 hit<-which(lookup$key==key & lookup$region_key==region_key)
 if(length(hit)==0L)hit<-which(lookup$base_key==key & lookup$region_key==region_key)
 if(length(hit)==1L)lookup$code[hit] else NA_character_
}
a$candidate<-mapply(candidate_code,a$key,a$region_key,USE.NAMES=FALSE)
a<-a %>% mutate(audit_class=case_when(
 name_missing~'Missing township name',exact_match~'Exact name match',
 key==normalise_name(name)~'Formatting-only difference',
 candidate==township_id~'Boundary primary-name match',
 !is.na(candidate) & candidate!=township_id~'Conflicting unique township label',
 TRUE~'Unresolved name'))
audit_summary<-a %>% group_by(audit_class) %>% summarise(records=n(),fatalities=sum(fatalities),.groups='drop')
name_pairs<-a %>% filter(name_flag) %>% count(admin1,admin3,region,name,audit_class,name='records',sort=TRUE)
# Geometry evidence for conflicting labels, without exposing incident coordinates.
conflicting<-a %>% filter(audit_class=='Conflicting unique township label')
if(nrow(conflicting)) {
 pts<-st_as_sf(conflicting,coords=c('longitude','latitude'),crs=4326) %>% st_transform(st_crs(g))
 conflict_distance<-as.numeric(st_distance(pts,g[match(conflicting$candidate,g$TS_PCODE),],by_element=TRUE))/1000
 conflicts<-conflicting %>% mutate(label_distance_km=conflict_distance,
   labelled_township=lookup$name[match(candidate,lookup$code)],
   adjacent=mapply(function(from,to)match(to,g$TS_PCODE)%in%s$nb[[match(from,g$TS_PCODE)]],township_id,candidate)) %>%
   group_by(admin3,name,region,labelled_township) %>% summarise(records=n(),fatalities=sum(fatalities),
    minimum_km=min(label_distance_km),maximum_km=max(label_distance_km),
    all_adjacent=all(adjacent),precise_records=sum(geo_precision==1),.groups='drop')
}else conflicts<-tibble()
unresolved<-a$audit_class %in% c('Missing township name','Conflicting unique township label','Unresolved name')
audit_sets<-list('Exclude unresolved or missing labels'=a[!unresolved,],
 'Exclude every initial name flag'=a[!a$name_flag,],
 'Use unique conflicting labels instead of coordinates'=a %>% mutate(township_id=if_else(
   audit_class=='Conflicting unique township label',candidate,township_id)))
lw<-nb2listw(s$nb,style='W',zero.policy=TRUE)
star<-nb2listw(include.self(s$nb),style='W',zero.policy=TRUE)
audit_results<-list();audit_counts<-list()
for(scenario in names(audit_sets)) {
 z<-audit_sets[[scenario]]
 totals<-z %>% group_by(township_id) %>% summarise(events=n(),fatalities=sum(fatalities),.groups='drop')
 audit_counts[[scenario]]<-tibble(scenario=scenario,retained=nrow(z),excluded=nrow(a)-nrow(z),
  relabelled=if(scenario=='Use unique conflicting labels instead of coordinates')nrow(conflicting) else 0L)
 for(v in c('events','fatalities')){
  x<-replace_na(totals[[v]][match(g$TS_PCODE,totals$township_id)],0)
  out<-local_results(x,lw,star)
  base<-s$static %>% filter(variable==v)
  audit_results[[paste(scenario,v)]]<-bind_cols(tibble(code=g$TS_PCODE,scenario=scenario,variable=v),out) %>%
   mutate(baseline_hot=base$gi_z>0 & base$gi_q<.05,hot=gi_z>0 & gi_q<.05,
    baseline_lisa=ifelse(base$moran_q<.05,base$lisa,'Not significant'),
    adjusted_lisa=ifelse(moran_q<.05,lisa,'Not significant'))
 }
}
audit_results<-bind_rows(audit_results)
audit_stability<-audit_results %>% group_by(scenario,variable) %>% summarise(
 baseline_n=sum(baseline_hot),alternative_hot=sum(hot),retained=sum(hot & baseline_hot),
 gained=sum(hot & !baseline_hot),lost=sum(!hot & baseline_hot),
 Jaccard=sum(hot & baseline_hot)/sum(hot|baseline_hot),
 lisa_label_changes=sum(adjusted_lisa!=baseline_lisa),.groups='drop') %>% rename(baseline_hot=baseline_n)

# Descriptive national comparison: constant-share benchmark, not a causal model.
national<-d$panel %>% group_by(month) %>% summarise(across(c(events,fatalities),sum),.groups='drop') %>%
 pivot_longer(c(events,fatalities),names_to='variable',values_to='national')
relative_series<-d$panel %>% pivot_longer(c(events,fatalities),names_to='variable',values_to='local') %>%
 left_join(national,by=c('month','variable')) %>% mutate(share=ifelse(national>0,local/national,NA_real_))
national_windows<-national %>% filter(as.integer(format(month,'%m'))<=9,format(month,'%Y')%in%c('2024','2025')) %>%
 group_by(variable,year=format(month,'%Y')) %>% summarise(total=sum(national),.groups='drop') %>%
 pivot_wider(names_from=year,values_from=total,names_prefix='national_') %>%
 mutate(national_growth_pct=100*(national_2025/national_2024-1))
relative_comparison<-relative_series %>% filter(as.integer(format(month,'%m'))<=9,format(month,'%Y')%in%c('2024','2025')) %>%
 group_by(township_id,variable,year=format(month,'%Y')) %>% summarise(total=sum(local),.groups='drop') %>%
 pivot_wider(names_from=year,values_from=total,names_prefix='local_') %>% left_join(national_windows,by='variable') %>%
 mutate(share_2024=100*local_2024/national_2024,share_2025=100*local_2025/national_2025,
 share_change_pp=share_2025-share_2024,expected_2025=local_2024/national_2024*national_2025,
 local_growth_pct=ifelse(local_2024>0,100*(local_2025/local_2024-1),NA_real_),
 relative_growth=ifelse(local_2024>0,(local_2025/local_2024)/(national_2025/national_2024),NA_real_))
case_comparison<-relative_comparison %>% inner_join(e$cases %>% select(code,case_id,township,region),by=c('township_id'='code')) %>% arrange(case_id,variable)
case_shares<-relative_series %>% inner_join(e$cases %>% select(code,case_id,township,region),by=c('township_id'='code')) %>%
 mutate(quarter=as.Date(paste0(format(month,'%Y'),'-',sprintf('%02d',3*((as.integer(format(month,'%m'))-1)%/%3)+1),'-01'))) %>%
 group_by(case_id,township,region,quarter,variable) %>% summarise(local=sum(local),national=sum(national),.groups='drop') %>%
 mutate(share_pct=100*local/national)

# Select the largest lower-of-two O/E ratios from the already supported set.
# A Jaccard ceiling prevents selecting nearly identical neighbourhoods.
pool<-e$severity %>% filter(excess,precise_excess) %>% mutate(minimum_ratio=pmin(ratio,precise_ratio)) %>%
 arrange(desc(minimum_ratio),code)
neighbours<-function(code)sort(unique(c(match(code,g$TS_PCODE),s$nb[[match(code,g$TS_PCODE)]])))
selected<-character()
for(code in pool$code){
 ids<-neighbours(code)
 overlaps<-vapply(selected,function(other){b<-neighbours(other);length(intersect(ids,b))/length(union(ids,b))},numeric(1))
 if(!length(overlaps)||all(overlaps<=.5))selected<-c(selected,code)
 if(length(selected)==3L)break
}
stopifnot(length(selected)==3L)
robust_cases<-pool %>% filter(code%in%selected) %>% arrange(match(code,selected)) %>% mutate(case_label=paste0('S',row_number()))
marked<-d$assigned %>% group_by(month,event_type) %>% mutate(expected_mark=mean(fatalities)) %>% ungroup()
decomposition<-list();annual<-list();concentration<-list();overlap<-list()
for(code in selected){
 z<-marked %>% filter(township_id%in%g$TS_PCODE[neighbours(code)])
 label<-robust_cases$township[match(code,robust_cases$code)]
 decomposition[[code]]<-z %>% group_by(event_type) %>% summarise(events=n(),observed=sum(fatalities),expected=sum(expected_mark),.groups='drop') %>%
  mutate(code=code,township=label,excess=observed-expected)
 annual[[code]]<-z %>% group_by(year=as.integer(format(month,'%Y'))) %>% summarise(events=n(),observed=sum(fatalities),expected=sum(expected_mark),.groups='drop') %>%
  mutate(code=code,township=label,excess=observed-expected)
 concentration[[code]]<-tibble(code=code,neighbour_townships=length(neighbours(code)),
  largest_incident_pct=100*max(z$fatalities)/sum(z$fatalities),
  largest_month_pct=100*max(tapply(z$fatalities,z$month,sum))/sum(z$fatalities),
  precise_incident_pct=100*mean(z$geo_precision==1),
  name_unresolved_records=sum(z$event_id_cnty%in%a$event_id_cnty[unresolved]))
}
robust_cases<-robust_cases %>% left_join(bind_rows(concentration),by='code')
for(i in seq_len(length(selected)-1))for(j in seq.int(i+1,length(selected))){
 ids<-neighbours(selected[i]);other<-neighbours(selected[j])
 overlap[[paste(i,j)]]<-tibble(first=robust_cases$township[i],second=robust_cases$township[j],
  shared_townships=length(intersect(ids,other)),Jaccard=length(intersect(ids,other))/length(union(ids,other)))
}
decomposition<-bind_rows(decomposition);annual<-bind_rows(annual)
drivers<-decomposition %>% group_by(code) %>% slice_max(excess,n=1,with_ties=FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
 left_join(robust_cases %>% select(code,total_excess=observed,expected_total=expected),by='code') %>%
 mutate(net_excess_share_pct=100*excess/(total_excess-expected_total))
peak_period<-annual %>% group_by(code) %>% slice_max(excess,n=1,with_ties=FALSE) %>% ungroup()
raw_hashes<-tools::md5sum(names(d$quality$hashes))
stopifnot(identical(unname(raw_hashes),unname(d$quality$hashes)))
result<-list(audit_summary=audit_summary,name_pairs=name_pairs,conflicts=conflicts,
 audit_counts=bind_rows(audit_counts),audit_results=audit_results,audit_stability=audit_stability,
 national_windows=national_windows,relative_comparison=relative_comparison,case_comparison=case_comparison,
 case_shares=case_shares,robust_cases=robust_cases,decomposition=decomposition,annual=annual,
 drivers=drivers,peak_period=peak_period,overlap=bind_rows(overlap))
saveRDS(result,'outputs/evidence_audit.rds')
for(item in c('audit_summary','name_pairs','conflicts','audit_stability','case_comparison','robust_cases','decomposition','annual'))
 write.csv(result[[item]],paste0('outputs/',item,'.csv'),row.names=FALSE,na='')
print(audit_summary);print(conflicts);print(audit_stability);print(national_windows)
print(case_comparison %>% select(township,variable,local_2024,local_2025,share_2024,share_2025,relative_growth))
print(robust_cases %>% select(case_label,township,region,ratio,precise_ratio,category,largest_incident_pct))

08_severity_validation.R

# Validate the previously selected cases without selecting replacement examples.
# Every randomisation and deletion scenario retains the full 330-test BH family.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr);library(sf);library(spdep)})
d<-readRDS('outputs/prepared.rds');s<-readRDS('outputs/statistics.rds')
h<-readRDS('outputs/evidence_audit.rds')
g<-d$townships;n<-nrow(g)
for(expr in parse('analysis/04_extensions.R')) {
 if(is.call(expr) && identical(expr[[1]],as.name('<-')) && is.symbol(expr[[2]]) &&
    as.character(expr[[2]])=='severity_test')eval(expr)
}
seeds<-c(20265001L,20265002L,20265003L)
B<-1999L
samples<-list('All assigned events'=d$assigned,
 'Precision code 1'=filter(d$assigned,geo_precision==1))
repeated<-list();deleted<-list();deletion_audit<-list()
for(sample_name in names(samples)){
 records<-samples[[sample_name]]
 for(seed in seeds){
  message('Severity seed check: ',sample_name,', seed ',seed)
  out<-severity_test(records,sample_name,B=B,seed=seed)
  repeated[[paste(sample_name,seed)]]<-out %>% mutate(seed=seed,
   supported=q<.05 & observed>expected)
 }
 for(code in h$robust_cases$code){
  ids<-sort(unique(c(match(code,g$TS_PCODE),s$nb[[match(code,g$TS_PCODE)]])))
  candidates<-records %>% filter(township_id%in%g$TS_PCODE[ids]) %>%
   arrange(desc(fatalities),event_id_cnty)
  stopifnot(nrow(candidates)>0,candidates$fatalities[1]>0)
  # Remove one record, using its ID only in memory to break tied maxima.
  reduced<-records %>% filter(event_id_cnty!=candidates$event_id_cnty[1])
  stopifnot(nrow(reduced)==nrow(records)-1L)
  message('Largest-incident deletion: ',sample_name,', focal code ',code)
  out<-severity_test(reduced,sample_name,B=B,seed=seeds[1])
  deleted[[paste(sample_name,code)]]<-out %>% mutate(deletion_case=.env$code,
   supported=q<.05 & observed>expected)
  deletion_audit[[paste(sample_name,code)]]<-tibble(scenario=sample_name,
   deletion_case=code,removed_records=1L,removed_fatalities=candidates$fatalities[1],
   before_records=nrow(records),after_records=nrow(reduced),
   before_fatalities=sum(records$fatalities),after_fatalities=sum(reduced$fatalities))
 }
}
repeated<-bind_rows(repeated);deleted<-bind_rows(deleted)
deletion_audit<-bind_rows(deletion_audit)
cases<-h$robust_cases %>% select(code,township,region)
seed_cases<-repeated %>% inner_join(cases,by='code') %>%
 group_by(code,township,scenario) %>% summarise(runs=n(),supported_runs=sum(supported),
 ratio=first(ratio),p_min=min(p),p_max=max(p),q_min=min(q),q_max=max(q),.groups='drop')
seed_families<-repeated %>% group_by(scenario,seed) %>% summarise(
 supported_neighbourhoods=sum(supported),.groups='drop')
deletion_cases<-deleted %>% filter(code==deletion_case) %>% inner_join(cases,by='code') %>%
 left_join(deletion_audit,by=c('scenario','deletion_case')) %>%
 select(code,township,scenario,observed,expected,ratio,p,q,supported,removed_fatalities)
stopifnot(nrow(seed_cases)==6,nrow(deletion_cases)==6,
 identical(unname(tools::md5sum(names(d$quality$hashes))),unname(d$quality$hashes)))
saveRDS(list(seeds=seeds,B=B,repeated=repeated,seed_cases=seed_cases,
 seed_families=seed_families,deleted=deleted,deletion_cases=deletion_cases,
 deletion_audit=deletion_audit),'outputs/severity_validation.rds')
write.csv(seed_cases,'outputs/severity_seed_checks.csv',row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(deletion_cases,'outputs/severity_deletion_checks.csv',row.names=FALSE)
print(seed_cases);print(seed_families);print(deletion_cases)

 if(is.call(expr) && identical(expr[[1]],as.name('<-')) && is.symbol(expr[[2]]) &&

}
test_pattern<-function(z,expected,tau=.3,p=.2){
 pp<-ifelse(z==0,1,.01)
 stopifnot(identical(classify_pattern(z,pp,tau,p),expected))
}
for(sign in c(1,-1)) {
 label<-if(sign==1)'hot spot' else 'cold spot'
 test_pattern(sign*c(rep(0,9),1),paste('New',label))
 test_pattern(sign*c(rep(0,8),1,1),paste('Consecutive',label))
 test_pattern(sign*c(0,1,rep(0,7),1),paste('Sporadic',label))
 test_pattern(sign*c(-1,rep(0,8),1),paste('New',label))
 test_pattern(sign*c(1,-1,rep(0,7),1),paste('Oscillating',label))
 test_pattern(sign*rep(1,10),paste('Persistent',label))
 test_pattern(sign*c(0,rep(1,9)),paste('Intensifying',label),tau=sign*.3,p=.01)
 test_pattern(sign*c(0,rep(1,9)),paste('Diminishing',label),tau=-sign*.3,p=.01)
 test_pattern(sign*c(rep(1,9),0),paste('Historical',label))
 test_pattern(sign*c(rep(1,8),0,0),'No pattern detected')
 test_pattern(sign*c(0,1,rep(0,8)),'No pattern detected')
}

for(k in seq_len(nrow(gs))) {
 row <- gs[k,]
 nb <- gm$sensitivity_graphs[[row$graph]]
 stopifnot(all(spdep::card(nb)>0),
  all(vapply(seq_along(nb),function(i) !(i %in% nb[[i]]),logical(1))))
 if(row$graph=='Symmetric 6-NN')stopifnot(all(vapply(seq_along(nb),
   function(i)all(vapply(nb[[i]],function(j)i %in% nb[[j]],logical(1))),logical(1))))
 lw <- spdep::nb2listw(nb,style='W')
 x <- d$townships[[row$variable]]
 if(row$transform=='log1p')x <- log1p(x)
 centered <- x-mean(x)
 direct <- length(x)/spdep::Szero(lw)*sum(centered*spdep::lag.listw(lw,centered))/sum(centered^2)
 stopifnot(abs(row$I-direct)<1e-12,
  row$min_neighbours==min(spdep::card(nb)),row$max_neighbours==max(spdep::card(nb)))
 set.seed(row$seed)
 rerun <- spdep::moran.mc(x,lw,nsim=9999,alternative='two.sided')
 null <- rerun$res[seq_len(9999)]
 observed <- as.numeric(rerun$statistic)
 pv <- min(1,2*min((1+sum(null>=observed))/10000,(1+sum(null<=observed))/10000))
 stopifnot(abs(pv-row$permutation_p)<1e-12)
 if(row$graph=='Queen' && row$transform=='Raw') {
  original <- gm$results[gm$results$variable==row$variable,]
  stopifnot(abs(original$I-row$I)<1e-12,original$permutation_p==row$permutation_p)
 }
}
cat('PASS: eight-setting global sensitivity, graph construction, Holm family and repeated permutations.\n')

# Research question and scope

Where do recorded armed-conflict events and reported fatalities cluster across Myanmar townships, and how did local concentrations evolve between January 2021 and September 2025?

The analysis distinguishes **absolute burden**, **spatial association**, and **temporal change in clustering**. A large count does not by itself establish a statistically significant hotspot. A hotspot does not establish why violence occurred. The intended use is retrospective peace-building and humanitarian situational awareness at township level, not targeting, tactical planning, or individual risk prediction.

This report follows the [Take-home Exercise 2 brief](https://isss626-ay2026-27aug.netlify.app/take-home_ex02). The companion [executive summary](executive_summary.qmd) presents the central findings. All outputs below derive from the supplied data rather than textbook example numbers.

# Data and study design

## Sources and variables

| Input | Role | Version and coverage |
|---|---|---|
| `data/Aspatial/ACLED_Data_Myanmar_Jan2021-Sep2025.csv` | Local ACLED extract for the course exercise | 1 January 2021 to 30 September 2025 |
| `data/Geospatial/mmr_polbnda_adm3_250k_mimu_1.shp` and companions | Township boundaries obtained through MIMU GeoNode | 330 unique township P-codes; embedded `PCode_V` is 9.4 |

The CSV contains violent and non-violent event types. The primary operational definition retains **Battles**, **Explosions/Remote violence**, and **Violence against civilians** within Myanmar. Protests, riots and strategic developments are excluded. This is an armed-conflict subset, not every event in ACLED's broader political-violence category. The latter can include specific protest and riot subtypes. See the [ACLED Codebook](https://acleddata.com/methodology/acled-codebook).

Two outcomes are analysed: the number of retained records and the sum of their reported fatalities. Fatalities represent recorded estimates, not an independently verified death toll. No population denominator is supplied, so neither outcome estimates per-capita risk. A zero bin means no retained record in this extract; it does not prove the absence of violence or complete reporting.

The boundary download request is preserved in `data/Geospatial/wfsrequest.txt`. The local file confirms the required version through its attributes. The source does not independently establish that every boundary reflects conditions in every study month. No download date is inferred from a file modification timestamp.

The course brief identifies eLearn as the distribution channel for its ACLED dataset. This report records the supplied filename and input fingerprint, but the local CSV alone does not verify its acquisition channel or download date. These provenance details require the original download record. The three retained event categories operationalise armed conflict consistently throughout the analysis.

## Data-quality checks and spatial assignment

The preparation script checks IDs, dates, coordinates, non-negative fatalities, boundary validity and township identifiers. It repairs geometries if necessary and transforms both polygons and points to a WGS84 Albers equal-area CRS centred on Myanmar. Coordinates are assigned through polygon intersection rather than joining potentially ambiguous township names. Repeated place names remain distinct through their P-codes.

```{r}
#| label: quality-table
kable(d$quality$audit,col.names=c('Check or processing stage','Records / units'),format.args=list(big.mark=','))
```

There are `r nrow(d$unassigned)` unassigned eligible records, all within one kilometre of the boundary. The primary analysis excludes these rather than silently snapping them. A sensitivity analysis assigns only these near-boundary records to their nearest polygon. Raw data remain unchanged. The main panel contains **`r fmt(nrow(d$assigned))` events** and **`r fmt(sum(d$assigned$fatalities))` reported fatalities**.

```{r}
kable(d$quality$precision,col.names=c('Geographic precision code','Temporal precision code','Assigned records'))
```

Geographic precision is not a distance-error estimate. The precise-location-only sensitivity retains code 1 and compares results with the full analysis. Among matched records, `r d$quality$name_check$missing_admin3` lack `admin3`; `r d$quality$name_check$exact_name_disagreement` have a township name that differs under a simple case-insensitive comparison. These flags can reflect transliteration, coding or location discrepancies. They are not automatically treated as incorrect spatial matches. Temporal precision limitations remain relevant even after monthly aggregation.

## Resolving the township-name flags

The initial string comparison is a screening device. Removing punctuation and spaces resolves **522** of the **530** non-missing name flags. A further **four** records use `Pangsang`, the primary name in the boundary label `Pangsang (Panghkam)`, within the same state. These are compatible labels, not demonstrated changes of township. **Four** records instead name a different, uniquely identified township in the same state. The **107** missing names remain a separate quality category. These classifications use only the supplied boundary names and state labels; no fuzzy spelling match or unsupported external crosswalk is used.

```{r}
kable(h$audit_summary,col.names=c('Diagnosis','Records','Reported fatalities'))
kable(h$name_pairs %>% mutate(admin3=replace_na(admin3,'[missing]')),
 col.names=c('ACLED state','ACLED township','Polygon state','Polygon township','Diagnosis','Records'))
```

The conflicting coordinates fall in Twantay rather than the label Kawhmu (two records), Pinlaung rather than Pekon (one), and Ann rather than Toungup (one). Distance below is from the recorded point to the labelled alternative polygon, not to a town centre. Proximity can indicate boundary or coding uncertainty but cannot determine which field is correct. Coordinates retain priority in the main analysis; alternate assignments are tested rather than written into the raw data.

```{r}
kable(h$conflicts %>% select(admin3,name,region,records,fatalities,minimum_km,maximum_km,precise_records),digits=3,
 col.names=c('Recorded label','Spatial match','State/region','Records','Fatalities','Min distance km','Max distance km','Precision-1 records'))
```

### Does the uncertainty change the static findings?

Three checks exclude the **111** unresolved/missing-name records, exclude all **637** initial flags (including harmless formatting differences), or assign the four conflicting records to their uniquely matched labels. Each check recomputes both outcomes with the original weights, seeds and 4,999 permutations. This is a targeted diagnostic of label uncertainty; it does not establish the correct location of an individual incident.

```{r}
kable(h$audit_counts,col.names=c('Scenario','Retained records','Excluded','Reassigned'))
kable(h$audit_stability,digits=3,
 col.names=c('Scenario','Outcome','Baseline BH hot','Alternative BH hot','Retained','Gained','Lost','Jaccard','BH LISA changes'))
```

All three scenarios retain the same **23 event** and **27 fatality** positive Gi* townships after BH adjustment. Their hotspot-set Jaccard similarity is **1.000**. The separate LISA-change column prevents hotspot agreement from being mistaken for agreement on every local statistic. This materially narrows the original concern: the flagged names do not drive these adjusted static hotspot sets. It does not validate every input record or establish EHSA robustness to reassignments. Aggregate diagnostics are saved without incident IDs, coordinates or narrative notes.

## A complete monthly space-time cube

The panel is the Cartesian product of 330 townships and 57 months: **18,810 bins**. A left join of observed aggregates followed by explicit zero-filling prevents inactive townships or months from disappearing. Assertions reconcile panel totals with the matched input records. The study ends in September 2025; full-year totals for 2025 would not be comparable with earlier full years.

```{r}
kable(head(d$panel,8),col.names=c('Township P-code','Month','Events','Reported fatalities'))
```

# Descriptive geography

![Township totals for the two conflict indicators.](outputs/figures/burden.png){#fig-burden}

Recorded burden is uneven. `r places(g$TS_PCODE[order(-g$events)],3)` have the largest event totals. The maps use a logarithmic colour transformation to show lower-count areas alongside large totals; the underlying counts are untransformed. Differences between event and fatality distributions can arise from the severity and composition of recorded incidents. These maps describe burden without testing clustering or controlling for population, land area, access or reporting intensity.

![National monthly series of spatially assigned records.](outputs/figures/monthly.png){#fig-monthly}

The peak event month is **`r format_month_en(f$monthly$month[which.max(f$monthly$events)])`**, with `r fmt(max(f$monthly$events))` records. The peak reported-fatality month is **`r format_month_en(f$monthly$month[which.max(f$monthly$fatalities)])`**. The separate axes avoid treating different units as interchangeable. National changes can affect a space-time statistic with a pooled temporal reference, so township trend findings require comparison with this common temporal context.

![Ten highest event totals with state or region labels.](outputs/figures/top_townships.png){#fig-top}

The ranking identifies places contributing most to the recorded national burden. It is useful for selecting case studies for contextual review, but does not rank residents' risk. A township can have a large total without being surrounded by similarly high-count neighbours; Local Moran's I below separates those situations.

# Spatial weights and inference

Queen contiguity represents shared boundaries or vertices, with a ten-metre tolerance after projection. Local Moran's I excludes the focal township; Gi* includes it. Row-standardised weights give each neighbourhood total weight one. A township with no queen neighbour receives a reciprocal link to its nearest representative point so it can participate in analysis. This exception is explicit and does not imply a transport connection across water.

```{r}
kable(data.frame(Measure=c('Minimum analysis neighbours','Median analysis neighbours','Maximum analysis neighbours','Queen isolates repaired','Original connected components','Analysis connected components'),Value=c(min(s$weights$analysis_neighbours),median(s$weights$analysis_neighbours),max(s$weights$analysis_neighbours),sum(s$weights$isolate_link_added),s$queen_components,s$analysis_components)))
```

Different graph components are retained rather than joined arbitrarily. Conditional permutations still use the national reference distribution. A symmetric six-nearest-neighbour graph provides a sensitivity check. Neither graph is a causal model of conflict diffusion.

Static tests use 4,999 conditional permutations and two-sided simulation p-values, a fixed seed and one core. Their null concerns spatial arrangement conditional on observed values and the selected neighbourhood. Local Moran categories combine the test with the signs of the centred focal value and spatial lag. Gi* uses self-including weights. The [spdep documentation](https://r-spatial.github.io/spdep/reference/localG.html) specifies this distinction.

Main maps colour only tests with **p < 0.05**, as requested. Grey polygons supply context, not a significant class. Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjusted values are reported separately for each outcome and test family. Spatial dependence and heavy-tailed counts limit simple inferential interpretations; significance is exploratory, not a causal or predictive guarantee.

Thin state/region outlines and selected labels on the main LMSA and EHSA maps provide geographic reference. These labels are not statistical findings and do not change the township unit of analysis. The case locator and neighbourhood maps identify the more detailed areas discussed later.

## Global context and Moran scatterplots

This supplementary step adapts the Global Moran's I workflow in [Hands-on Exercise 5(1)](../../Hands-on_Ex/Hands-on_Ex05/Hands-on_Ex0501.qmd) and the centred scatterplot in [Hands-on Exercise 5(2)](../../Hands-on_Ex/Hands-on_Ex05/Hands-on_Ex0502.qmd), based on the course's [Chapter 9](https://r4gdsa.netlify.app/chap09.html) and [Chapter 10](https://r4gdsa.netlify.app/chap10.html). Hunan GDPPC is replaced by the two Myanmar township totals. The existing queen-based graph, isolate repairs, township order and row standardisation are retained; the focal township is excluded.

The null randomly reallocates the observed totals across the fixed national graph. Each outcome uses 9,999 permutations and a fixed seed, with the null statistics generated by [moran.mc](https://r-spatial.github.io/spdep/reference/moran.mc.html). To avoid a zero simulated p-value, the reported two-sided p is twice the smaller inclusive tail probability, capped at one; each tail is (1 + number of equally or more extreme simulations) / 10,000. This explicit finite-simulation convention replaces the function's returned p-value. Holm adjustment covers these **two global tests only**, separately from the existing local BH families. Under random allocation the expected I is -1/329, not exactly zero. This is a supplementary overall check, not a prerequisite for local analysis or a replacement for EHSA.

```{r}
#| label: global-moran-table
global_table <- global_moran$results %>%
  transmute(Outcome=ifelse(variable=='events','Event counts','Reported fatalities'),
            `Moran I`=round(I,4),`Null expectation`=round(null_expectation,4),
            `Permutation p`=sprintf('%.4f',permutation_p),
            `Holm p (2 tests)`=sprintf('%.4f',holm_p),Permutations=permutations)
kable(global_table)
```

Both outcomes show positive overall spatial association at the two-test Holm 0.05 threshold. The larger fatality I does not establish a statistically tested difference between outcomes. Population, reporting coverage and other spatial heterogeneity can violate the national exchangeability assumption; these are count-based associations, not per-capita risks or causal effects.

![Moran scatterplots for both outcomes, using the same weights and totals as the existing local analysis.](outputs/figures/global_moran_scatter.png){#fig-global-moran}

Each point is a township. The axes show its standardised total and the neighbour average of **the same standardised variable**. The line through the origin has slope I because the weights sum to 330. Colours distinguish descriptive quadrants; triangles identify existing local Moran BH q < 0.05 results. Quadrant membership alone does not establish significance. Both panels use the same axis scales and raw totals before standardisation.

### Sensitivity to skewness and spatial weights

For each outcome, a two-by-two comparison crosses raw totals and `log1p(total)` with the original queen graph and a symmetric six-nearest-neighbour graph. The latter uses the same projected representative points as the existing local sensitivity analysis. Symmetrisation retains an edge selected by either township, so final degrees can exceed six. All graphs exclude self-neighbours and use row-standardised weights. The transformation retains zeros and reduces the influence of large totals, but changes the measured variable and does not adjust for population or reporting.

Each setting uses 9,999 permutations and the same outcome-specific seed. Holm adjustment jointly covers **all eight outcome/setting tests**, including the two original raw/queen tests. The earlier two-test adjusted values remain labelled separately; none is substituted into local or EHSA results.

```{r}
#| label: global-moran-sensitivity
global_sensitivity <- global_moran$sensitivity
kable(global_sensitivity %>%
  transmute(Outcome=ifelse(variable=='events','Events','Fatalities'),
            Weights=graph,Scale=transform,`Moran I`=round(I,3),
            `Permutation p`=sprintf('%.4f',permutation_p),
            `Holm p (8 tests)`=sprintf('%.4f',holm_p_8)))
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
cat(sprintf('Positive association remains supported in %s of %s settings after eight-test Holm adjustment. ',
            sum(global_sensitivity$positive_supported),nrow(global_sensitivity)))
for(v in c('events','fatalities')) {
  a <- global_sensitivity %>% filter(variable==v)
  cat(sprintf('%s I ranges from %.3f to %.3f. ',if(v=='events')'Event-count' else 'Fatality',min(a$I),max(a$I)))
}
```

The direction and significance survive reduced count skewness and an alternative graph. Magnitudes change, so they should not be treated as directly comparable effect sizes across scales or weights. These related checks are not independent replications, do not prove that extreme observations have no influence, and do not validate local or temporal classifications. All eight simulated p-values reach the doubled-tail floor of 0.0002; the common adjusted value of 0.0016 reflects simulation resolution, not identical strength of evidence.

# Emerging hot spot analysis

## Space-time neighbourhood and classification

For each township-month, the Gi* neighbourhood contains the focal township and its spatial neighbours in the current month and the preceding month. January 2021 has no earlier bin and uses its current-month neighbourhood only. This is a retrospective, one-lag specification, not a forecasting model. Row standardisation accounts for differing neighbourhood sizes. The reference is the complete study cube, so national temporal change can contribute to local trends.

Space-time Gi* uses 999 conditional permutations with the focal observation fixed. A compiled Rcpp helper samples distinct non-focal bins by rejection sampling, avoiding full-population shuffles for every sparse neighbourhood. The two-sided p-value is twice the smaller inclusive-tail count, with a plus-one correction, capped at one. This handles ties conservatively. The helper was checked against exhaustive enumeration on a small graph; its Gi* z-values are computed by `spdep::localG`. Significant positive and negative bins define hot and cold episodes. A Mann-Kendall test of each township's 57 Gi* z-values measures monotonic change in clustering strength. Its tau is an ordinal association, not an events-per-month growth rate.

Sign-specific rules distinguish new, consecutive, intensifying, diminishing, persistent, historical, sporadic and oscillating patterns. For persistent/intensifying/diminishing patterns, at least 90% of bins must be significant in the same direction. The classification uses the versioned [ArcGIS Pro 3.4 pattern definitions](https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/3.4/tool-reference/space-time-pattern-mining/learnmoreemerging.htm), implemented explicitly in R. In particular, **a sporadic hot or cold spot must be significant in the same direction in September 2025**, have an earlier same-sign episode, fewer than 90% same-sign bins, and no opposite-sign episode. Earlier intermittent episodes with a non-significant final bin do not qualify. This definition differs from older documentation that omitted the terminal requirement.

The R workflow follows these pattern definitions but uses its own permutation-based inference. It does not reproduce ArcGIS numerically. The primary maps use nominal bin p-values to make the exercise's p < 0.05 threshold explicit. A separate sensitivity analysis classifies BH-adjusted bins, because the documented ArcGIS workflow uses multiple-testing correction. The two inference conventions must not be conflated.

The map additionally requires **Mann-Kendall p < 0.05** and a recognised pattern. A persistent hotspot without a significant trend can therefore be present in the full results but grey on this significance-filtered map. That is an intentional distinction between persistent clustering and evidence of change.

![Space-time Gi* trajectories for high-burden townships.](outputs/figures/gi_heatmap.png){#fig-heatmap}

The heatmap contrasts clustering strength through time for the twenty highest-count townships. Its colours show z-values rather than a significance mask. It helps distinguish sustained concentrations from brief episodes before looking at the final classifications. Selection by total burden means this view is illustrative rather than representative of all townships.

Positive tau indicates increasing Gi* values, which can mean intensifying high-value clustering or weakening low-value clustering. Negative tau has the reverse interpretation. The class label and the sign of Gi* must therefore be read together.',sum(ee$mk_p<.05),sum(ee$map_class!='Not displayed')))

cat(sprintf('%s townships meet the Mann-Kendall threshold for reported fatalities, of which %s also have a recognised pattern. This map assesses changes in the spatial concentration of recorded fatalities. ## Pattern-by-pattern findings

Each row below is a short description of a displayed pattern, including its geographic examples. Counts refer to townships, not conflict events. Full classifications and test statistics are available in `outputs/ehsa_statistics.csv`.

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
pattern_table<-s$ehsa %>% filter(map_class!='Not displayed') %>% group_by(variable,map_class) %>% summarise(townships=n(),examples=places(code,3),.groups='drop')
kable(pattern_table,col.names=c('Outcome','Pattern','Townships','Examples'))
```

New patterns appear only in the final significant bin. Consecutive patterns form a single terminal run of at least two months, with no earlier significant bin of the same sign. Intensifying and diminishing patterns show significant directional change within a long-standing hot/cold concentration. Historical patterns lose their significant terminal status after a high share of earlier significant bins. Oscillating patterns include an earlier opposite-sign episode and a significant final bin. Sporadic patterns recur intermittently, end in a significant same-sign bin and contain no opposite-sign episode. The explicit precedence is new, long-standing, consecutive, oscillating and sporadic. These rules summarise observed sequences rather than predict future conflict. Automated tests cover both signs, the 90% boundary and non-significant final months.

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
pattern_explanation<-c(
 'Sporadic hot spot'='High-value episodes recur intermittently and the final month is hot. This supports a terminal concentration, but not sustained intensification throughout the study.',
 'Oscillating hot spot'='The terminal hot episode follows an earlier cold episode. This changing sign argues against describing the entire period as uniformly high-conflict.',
 'Sporadic cold spot'='Low-value clustering recurs intermittently and the final month is cold relative to the pooled reference. This is neither proof of safety nor necessarily a decline in absolute events.',
 'Intensifying cold spot'='At least 90% of months are cold and the Gi* trend becomes more negative. This is strengthening low-value clustering, not intensifying violence.',
 'Consecutive cold spot'='A previously absent same-sign pattern forms an uninterrupted cold run at the end of the study. Its persistence beyond September 2025 is unknown.',
 'Oscillating cold spot'='The terminal cold episode follows earlier hot clustering. This indicates a change in relative concentration, not demonstrated conflict resolution.')
for(j in seq_len(nrow(pattern_table))){
 row<-pattern_table[j,]
 part<-s$ehsa %>% filter(variable==row$variable,map_class==row$map_class)
 regions<-sort(table(g$ST[match(part$code,g$TS_PCODE)]),decreasing=TRUE)
 region_text<-paste(paste0(names(head(regions,2)),' (',as.integer(head(regions,2)),')'),collapse=' and ')
 cat(sprintf('\n\n### %s: %s\n\n',if(row$variable=='events')'Event counts' else 'Reported fatalities',row$map_class))
 cat(sprintf('This pattern covers %s townships; the largest regional counts are %s. %s Of these townships, %s also pass the three-month-block trend check and %s survive BH adjustment of the Mann-Kendall tests. The pattern is descriptive and its nominal trend significance should not override these uncertainty checks.\n\n',nrow(part),region_text,pattern_explanation[[row$map_class]],sum(part$block_p<.05),sum(part$mk_q<.05)))
}
```

# Robustness and uncertainty

## Multiple testing

```{r}
kable(s$inference,col.names=c('Outcome','Moran p < .05','Moran BH q < .05','Gi* p < .05','Gi* BH q < .05'))
kable(s$ehsa_summary,col.names=c('Outcome','MK p < .05','MK BH q < .05','Also supported by block test','Displayed EHSA patterns'))
```

![Event-count Gi* evidence before and after BH adjustment.](outputs/figures/multiplicity.png){#fig-multiplicity}

The darker areas retain statistical support after adjusting the static event-count Gi* family. Nominal-only areas deserve more cautious interpretation. BH adjustment is a useful sensitivity check, not a correction for geolocation errors, uneven reporting or a misspecified neighbourhood. The unadjusted task maps should not be described as confirmed findings merely because they satisfy p < 0.05.

## Neighbourhood, geolocation and temporal dependence

```{r}
kable(s$sensitivity_summary,digits=3,col.names=c('Alternative','Moran class agreement','Gi* class agreement','Hot spots'))
```

Agreement compares all township labels, including non-significant ones, so it can be high even when some hotspots change. The six-nearest-neighbour graph tests the spatial definition; the precision-code-1 subset changes both location quality and sample composition; the one-kilometre reassignment tests the eight near-boundary exclusions. None is automatically a superior truth.

Neighbourhoods overlap in time and Gi* series can be serially correlated. The conventional Mann-Kendall p-value assumes temporal independence. The extended checks use **999 permutations each of consecutive 3-, 6- and 12-month blocks**, preserving order within each block and comparing absolute tau. A shorter final block is retained when the width does not divide 57. The plus-one p-value has resolution 0.001. These checks assume blocks are exchangeable under the null. They do not fully correct seasonality, non-stationarity or long-range dependence. In particular, the 12-month version has only five blocks and limited distinct rearrangements.

### Temporal evidence after sensitivity checks

```{r}
kable(e$temporal_summary,col.names=c('Outcome','MK p < .05','3-month support','6-month support','12-month support','BH + all blocks','Displayed patterns','Supported displayed'))
```

![Additional trend support for the corrected EHSA maps.](outputs/figures/trend_robustness.png){#fig-trend-robustness}

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
for(v in c('events','fatalities')) {
 a<-e$temporal_summary %>% filter(variable==v)
 cat(sprintf('For %s, %s of %s displayed patterns also meet MK BH q < 0.05 and all three block thresholds. ',if(v=='events')'event counts' else 'reported fatalities',a$supported_displayed,a$displayed))
}
cat('Teal identifies this additional support; orange identifies dependence on the trend-testing assumptions. This intersection is a conservative sensitivity screen, not a calibrated joint p-value or proof of persistence. Grey combines unrecognised patterns and non-significant trends, rather than certifying an absence of conflict.')
```

### Temporal neighbourhood and bin adjustment

The baseline includes the current and previous month. Alternative models use the current month only, or the current plus two preceding months. Each repeats the Gi* simulation and pattern classification using the same spatial graph and seed. A fourth comparison retains the baseline z-values but replaces bin p-values with BH q-values across all 18,810 bins, separately for each outcome. It does not adjust the MK family a second time.

```{r}
kable(e$scenario_summary,digits=3,col.names=c('Outcome','Alternative','Full-class agreement','Displayed patterns','Same displayed pattern retained','Baseline displayed'))
```

Full-class agreement includes unclassified townships and can overstate stability. The retained-pattern column instead asks whether each baseline displayed township keeps exactly the same label. A changed label can reflect altered significance or a changed sequence of episodes. No scenario is selected because it produces more significant results. Complete township transitions are exported to `outputs/ehsa_sensitivity.csv`.

The sensitivity is material: after adjusting the baseline space-time bins, **`r sum(e$comparison$scenario=='BH-adjusted space-time bins' & e$comparison$variable=='events' & e$comparison$map_class!='Not displayed')` event** and **`r sum(e$comparison$scenario=='BH-adjusted space-time bins' & e$comparison$variable=='fatalities' & e$comparison$map_class!='Not displayed')` fatality** trend-pattern combinations remain displayed. This does not imply that recorded fatalities are absent or spatially random. It means the terminal-bin and sequence rules no longer produce displayed fatality classifications under that more stringent inference convention. The nominal EHSA maps should therefore be treated as exploratory, especially for fatalities.

### Stability of the actual hotspot sets

```{r}
kable(e$spatial_summary,digits=3,col.names=c('Outcome','Alternative','Baseline hot','Alternative hot','Retained','Gained','Lost','Jaccard'))
```

Jaccard similarity is the number of shared hot townships divided by the number hot in either analysis. Unlike overall label agreement, it excludes agreements between two non-hot labels. Both outcomes now receive the six-neighbour, precision-code-1 and boundary checks. Removing imprecisely located events also changes coverage and sample size, so it is a sensitivity analysis rather than an automatic improvement in truth.

A difference between significance labels is not itself a statistically significant difference between the outcomes. Both tests reuse the same incident records, and the comparison remains descriptive. The four numbered locations are examined below.',get_n('Both outcomes'),get_n('Events only'),get_n('Fatalities only')))
